(a) THE TWO COMMAND LINES. 26a: in 'the findings file, snapshot_id', out 'the harness report'; 29a: 'python -m harness.score <findings> <cases>' -> {hits}. 13's row says the two are harmonised first and no page says how. Built as one command: two arguments print {hits} (29a), the same with --snapshot DOCUMENT --tree DIR prints the report (26a). 26a's input has no cases and no tree; the report cannot be made without the cases, and test 6 cannot be judged without the tree's bytes. (b) TEST 6, 'a ref outside the manifest or whose hash does not match'. A finding's evidence_refs carry {path, line_start, line_end} and no hash (26, 13d). Built: outside = the path is not a file of the snapshot document's manifest; hash = the finding's snapshot_id is not the document's (snapshot_mismatch), or the bytes read at the path do not hash to the manifest's value (ref_hash_mismatch); added: a line beyond the file's end (ref_line_missing). Which of these the page means is not said. (c) IDENTITY. tohum/07 and 13d give the fingerprint's formula (property + file + symbol + normalize(claim); without a symbol: rule + enclosing symbol or file + normalize(line content)) but not normalize, the encoding or the hash, nor who computes it; no code writes a finding yet. The scorer reads the finding's own fingerprint field and does not derive or check it; it only refuses one fingerprint carried by findings of two files, symbols, properties, tools or rules (fingerprint_conflict). Consequence, stated in the module: findings on different lines of one file and rule that carry one fingerprint are one finding (in clean_findings too), whoever wrote that fingerprint. Asked: the exact derivation and its owner (the registry's intake), so the scorer can check it against the snapshot's bytes. (d) A re-observation (same fingerprint again) is not read to match: only the first observation's references can hit. 13e does not say which observation scores. (e) 'A finding takes at most one case, a case once': built as a maximum matching, so the hit count does not depend on the order of the findings; a greedy first-fit reading gives a lower count on some inputs (test_score.Match). (f) POLICY KEYS. 18a lists constitutional.confidence_level (0,90 one-sided), stage_params.census_min_groups (45 'or all there are') and stage_params.match_window_lines (15); /work/logs/policy.json holds none of the three (its stage_params has rival_min_attempts and repeat_reject_limit only), and 29v's reader (policy.reads PATHS) has no path for them. So alpha, min_groups and window are arguments of the scorer and the live caller (yaz) gives none: recall_lb is null on the live line, a census with no miss is UNMEASURABLE (min_groups_unknown), K3+ cases match by symbol only. Related: spec-071. (g) THE VERDICT. 13e gives the census gate (every rule covered, no miss) and 19 says an insufficient sample is UNMEASURABLE; no page says what the scorer's verdict is for a dev run, for a class without a census, or how 'or all there are' is judged. Built: no case UNMEASURABLE; a class outside K0-K2 UNMEASURABLE; a miss FAIL; no miss PASS only when the caller's floor of groups is given and met. (h) CENSUS. 13e names K0, K1, K2 and K4; the hit rule matches K4 by property and window (it is 'K3 and above'), and no page says what a K4 'rule' is: the census is built for K0-K2 with rule = (tool, rule_id) among the cases scored; K4 has none. 'rules_total' is read as the rules among the cases, not the tool's whole catalog; 'rules_covered' as the rules with no missed case. (i) clean_findings is reported when the case list is empty (the snapshot document does not say whether it is clean, 13c), null otherwise; refused findings are counted in it (13e: none is left out). precision, precision_lb, unresolved, cost_usd, value_per_usd are null: nothing triages a finding that hit no case and no hunter run has a cost in P1. run_id, spec_version, hunter_id, prompt_sha256, rung are the caller's and null on the live line. (j) 29a's example line shows cp_lower's output as {"lb": "0.962400"}; the bound at (60, 60, 0,10) is 0,1^(1/60) = 0,962351 to six decimals, which is what the command prints; the table's four decimals (0,9624) agree by rounding, not by cutting. If the vector compares by cutting to four decimals, (60, 60) and others will differ; the page says 'compared with the table's number of digits' and not how. ON THE LIVE PATH: yaz scores the cycle's findings against the cycle's dev cases; the findings are none until an organ's output is kept (lint.discover), so every live report today is recall 0 with a case and UNMEASURABLE without.
